member.summary: Undefined.

member.summary: No interpolation is performed between frames, so a component's position changes from one frame to the next without any movement in between frames.

member.name: F:VisualComponents.Create3D.MotionPathInterpolation.Linear
member.summary: The path is interpolated as straight lines between the frames.

member.name: F:VisualComponents.Create3D.MotionPathInterpolation.Cubic
member.summary: A cubic spline is used to interpolate the path from one frame to the next.

member.name: T:VisualComponents.Create3D.IMotionPath
member.summary: Base interface for motion path behaviors.

member.name: P:VisualComponents.Create3D.IMotionPath.Acceleration
member.summary: Gets or sets acceleration rate of components on the path, in millimeters per second squared. If this is zero, acceleration is not calculated.

member.name: P:VisualComponents.Create3D.IMotionPath.Deceleration
member.summary: Gets or sets deceleration rate of components on the path, in millimeters per second squared. If this is zero, deceleration is not calculated.

member.name: P:VisualComponents.Create3D.IMotionPath.Accumulate
member.summary: Determines whether components on the path accumulate when one or more components are blocked at the end of the path. If true, components behind a blocked component keep moving until they hit the blocked component. If false, all components in the path stop when the end is blocked.

member.name: P:VisualComponents.Create3D.IMotionPath.Interpolation
member.summary: Gets or sets interpolation mode to use with the path frames.

member.name: P:VisualComponents.Create3D.IMotionPath.PathLength
member.summary: Gets the total length of the path.

member.name: P:VisualComponents.Create3D.IMotionPath.RetainOffset
member.summary: Determines how components are positioned on the path when they enter the path. If true, the component offset is retained, otherwise the component is placed with its origin at the nearest point on the path.

member.name: P:VisualComponents.Create3D.IMotionPath.SegmentSize
member.summary: Gets or sets conveyor segment size. If this is greater to zero, the conveyor is divided into segments of the given size, each of which may contain at most one component at any one time. The total number of segments will then determine the maximum capacity of the conveyor in addition to the property and any associated capacity controllers.
member.remarks: When this value is greater to zero, a contained component will not move into the next segment until the previous component has left it completely.

member.name: P:VisualComponents.Create3D.IMotionPath.SpaceUtilization
member.summary: Determines if components are kept apart from each other in accumulating mode, or when new components are added to the path. If set to false, components may overlap. This may be useful when is true and the components are spread out along the width of a conveyor. In this case two components are allowed to be side by side on the conveyor.

member.name: P:VisualComponents.Create3D.IMotionPath.DetailCurveMotion
member.summary: Determines if parts use at curved areas bound box information to avoid box shaped parts to intersect at corners. In some cases like when parts are cylindrical shapes this can cause extra spacing between parts in the curves and in these cases option could be disabled. Part starting movement at curve area after linear section will slow down slightly part immediately behind (at linear section) when part bound box starts rotating. If slight intersection temporarily in the transition from linear section to curved section is not a problem or is part shapes are cylindrical or similar then this option could be disabled.

member.name: P:VisualComponents.Create3D.IMotionPath.Speed
member.summary: Gets or sets the speed of the conveyor, in millimeters per second.

member.name: P:VisualComponents.Create3D.IMotionPath.Path
member.summary: Gets the ordered list of frames that define the path. The actual path is then calculated by interpolating using the method defined by property.

member.name: P:VisualComponents.Create3D.IMotionPath.Sensors
member.summary: Gets the list of sensors that are used in this path.

member.summary: Gets the path distance at the path position. If the position is outside the path then the distance at closest path position is returned.
member.returns: Path distance at the given position

member.name: T:VisualComponents.Create3D.IFeature
member.summary: Interface that represents simulation node feature tree objects. Features define the geometry of objects either by themselves or as a result of operations on other features. The result of the feature tree evaluation is placed in to the geometry container in ISimNode. This process is governed by properties in the feature objects, which are accessible through this class. Only the Geometry feature has a specific Python class vcGeometryFeature which is derived from vcFeature in order to support creation of custom geometry. All other features can be manipulated through the generic IFeature interface.
member.remarks: Assuming that SimNode.Geometry.Container is shared between all SimNodes and root feature is pointing to it. This is the only way feature can be manipulated as normal visual object.

member.name: T:VisualComponents.Create3D.IGeometryFeature
member.summary: Geometry feature interface

remarks.para: The Geometry feature stores generic geometry in the model. When geometry is imported from a geometry file, it is stored in a Geometry feature.
This is also the feature that is created when a feature sub tree is collapsed.
When a component is saved, geometries are stored inside a component file (*.vcm file) in a file format that best matches the geometry.

member.name: P:VisualComponents.Create3D.IGeometryFeature.CreaseAngle
member.summary:
Adjacent polygons whose angle difference is less than the CreaseAngle value will be treated as one smooth surface during light calculations, with their normals averaged to provide reflection normals.
A low value here will make the geometry appear faceted, while a high value will make it appear smooth.

member.name: T:VisualComponents.Create3D.IWedgeFeature
member.summary: Wedge feature interface

remarks.para: The Wedge geometry primitive generates a wedge-like shape with the specified dimensions.
The basic shape is a cuboid that is truncated with a plane parallel to the Y axis that intersects the far X-Y (top) and Y-Z (front) faces, at specified distances along the X and Z axes, respectively.
This shape may then be reflected through the X-Y (bottom) plane, the Y-Z (back) plane, or both.

member.name: T:VisualComponents.Create3D.IdentityMap
member.summary: Internal wrapper utility class.

remarks.para: This class manages wrapper instances to Revolution.dll native objects, so that there is only one wrapper instance for each object at any one time.

The wrapper objects must implement IWrapper, and they are stored with weak references, so they may be garbage collected if there are no other instances. This allows native objects that are kept alive only by being referenced from the .NET side to be cleaned up.

member.name: M:VisualComponents.Create3D.IdentityMap.GetOrCreate``1(System.IntPtr,System.Func{System.IntPtr,``0})
member.summary: Retrieves a wrapper for a native object. If there is no wrapper, one will be created using the given creation method.

member.name: M:VisualComponents.Create3D.IdentityMap.Get``1(System.IntPtr)
member.summary: Retrieve an existing wrapper for a native object. If there is none, null is returned.
member.remarks: This method tries to look up parent types of T if a wrapper for T is not available.

member.name: M:VisualComponents.Create3D.IdentityMap.GetOrCreateNoProxies``1(System.IntPtr,System.Func{System.IntPtr,``0})
member.summary: Get or create wrapper object without attaching debug proxies.

member.name: M:VisualComponents.Create3D.IdentityMap.GetOrCreate``1(System.IntPtr)
member.summary: Retrieves a wrapper for a native object. If there is no wrapper, one will be created using the IntPtr constructor of T.
member.remarks: Slower version to use from c++/cli as Func<IntPtr, T> can't be created in c++/cli. This method requires that T has a constructor that accepts a single IntPtr argument.

member.name: M:VisualComponents.Create3D.IdentityMap.RemoveWrapperIdentity(VisualComponents.Create3D.IWrapper)
member.summary: Remove wrapper from list.

remarks.para: This method removes all type mappings that point to the given wrapper instance.

This is typically triggered by rObject::InvalidateWrappers, when the native object is deleted. The only exception is PropertyWrappers for dynamically created/loaded properties. Those wrappers increase the reference count of native variable and force keep it in memory, until wrapper is collected by garbage collector, or until IdentityMap is cleared (and wrapper's Dispose() and ReleaseNativeResources() methods are called).

member.name: M:VisualComponents.Create3D.IdentityMap.DisposeAll
member.summary: Disposes and clears all wrappers in the list. Called on application shutdown.

member.name: M:VisualComponents.Create3D.IdentityMap.ClearDeleted
member.summary: Remove invalidated wrapper references from list.

member.name: M:VisualComponents.Create3D.IdentityMap.Clear
member.summary: Clean up unused wrappers.

member.summary: Node's material is not used.

member.name: F:VisualComponents.Create3D.MaterialInheritance.Inherit
member.summary: Node's material is inherited to geometries in the node and its child nodes that do not force their own materials

member.name: F:VisualComponents.Create3D.MaterialInheritance.ForceInherit
member.summary: Node's material is inherited to geometries in the node and all its child nodes.

member.name: F:VisualComponents.Create3D.MaterialInheritance.InheritNode
member.summary: Node's material is inherited to all geometries in the node that do not do not force their own materials

member.name: F:VisualComponents.Create3D.MaterialInheritance.ForceInheritNode
member.summary: Node's material is inherited to all geometries in this node.

member.name: F:VisualComponents.Create3D.MaterialInheritance.InheritLevel
member.summary: Node's material is inherited to all geometries on the same level that do not force their own materials. If node is world root then all the nodes in the world will be affected. If node is a component then all the nodes inside the component will be affected. Otherwise, only the node itself will be affected.

member.name: F:VisualComponents.Create3D.MaterialInheritance.ForceInheritLevel
member.summary: Node's material is inherited to all geometries on the same level. If node is world root then all the nodes in the world will be affected. If node is a component then all the nodes inside the component will be affected. Otherwise, only the node itself will be affected.

member.summary: Pack folder interface.
member.remarks: A pack folder is a set of files included in a component or layout file. When the folder is mapped, a folder is created in temporary storage, and all these files are extracted there. When the component or layout is saved, any files or folders in this area are stored as well.

member.summary: Current pack folder state.

member.summary: Local path where pack folder files can be found.
member.remarks: This is empty if the pack folder is not mapped.

member.name: M:VisualComponents.Create3D.IPackFolder.MapFolder(System.String)
member.summary: Unpack the files in the pack folder to a local folder.

remarks.para: The localPath argument is optional; if it is null or empty, the pack folder will be mapped to a location in the system temporary folder. In any case, the local folder location can be read in PackFolderLocalPath after calling this method.
Note that the given local path must exist when this method is called. Note also that this method will delete all files in the given folder before unpacking the packed files.

member.name: M:VisualComponents.Create3D.IPackFolder.RemapFolder(System.String)
member.summary: Change pack folder mapping without extracting or copying files.

remarks.para: This method maps the pack folder to a local path without replacing the files at the target local path.
Note that the given local path must exist when this method is called.

member.name: M:VisualComponents.Create3D.IPackFolder.RollbackFolder
member.summary: Remove local folder mapping without saving any changes.
member.remarks: The component pack folder will revert to the state before MapFolder was called.

member.summary: Whether the property is internally defined.

member.summary: Whether the property is intended for component design time use only.

Setting this property in internal property objects is not allowed.

member.name: P:VisualComponents.Create3D.IProperty.IsPersistent
member.summary: Whether the property is saved with the component or layout.

remarks.para: Persisted properties are written to the component or layout file when the file is saved.
In the case of custom properties, if IsPersistent is false, the property is not written at all, and will not be present once the component or layout is reloaded from file.
For internal properties, a non-persistent property may or may not be present after reloading. In case it is present, the value is typically reset to a default value.
Setting this property on internal property objects is not allowed.

member.summary: Property container interface.

remarks.para: This is implemented by object that have a list of dynamic properties that may or may not be extended.

member.name: M:VisualComponents.Create3D.IPropertyContainer.CreateProperty(System.Type,VisualComponents.Create3D.PropertyConstraintType)
member.summary: Create a property object that can be used with the property container.
member.para: The CreateProperty method creates a property object that is compatible with the property container.
To create a simple property, use one of the following types:

item.description: Integer value. All constraint types are supported.
Real value. All constraint types are supported.
String value. AllowedValueSet constraint is supported.
Boolean value. Does not support constraints.
Vector value. AllowedValueSet constraint is supported.
Matrix value. AllowedValueSet constraint is supported.

member.para: To specify a reference type, specify the type of a wrapper interface. Reference parameters are always constrainted with AllowedValueSet.
List properties can be created by using an array type. Constraints are not supported.
Note that not all property containers support all property types.
member.remarks: The property is not automatically added to the container, so that has to be done separately, by adding it to the Properties list.
member.exception: Thrown if the given value type, constraint type, and/or combination of these is not supported by the property container.
Thrown if the property container cannot be modified.

member.name: T:VisualComponents.Create3D.IRecordListProperty
member.summary: Record list property interface.

remarks.para: A record list property contains a list of records, which are collections of name-value pairs. The record list property interface extends the list property interface where the element value type is a tuple containing a string (name) and an object (value.)
An individual record is usually based on a pre-defined template, which is a set of pre-defined properties that must exist in the record.

Depending on the record list property, it may also support free-form records. A free-form record is not based on a template, but can contain any properties, as determined by creating them when the record is created.
Some record templates also allow custom properties to be added in addition to those defined by the template.

member.summary: Interface for objects that can share data when being cloned.

member.name: P:VisualComponents.Create3D.ISharedCloneable.IsSharedClone
member.summary: Indicates if this object shares data with another object.

remarks.para: A shared clone uses less memory than a clone with its own copy of the data, but is also limited in that some settings are shared as well.

A component that is a shared clone shares the feature tree and node structures. In practice, this means that a component must be made unique before changing any features, or changing any parameters that cause a component rebuild, otherwise all components that have the same sharing ID (i.e. share the same data) are affected.

member.name: P:VisualComponents.Create3D.ISharedCloneable.SharingId
member.summary: Sharing ID of the shared data.
member.remarks: Objects with the same sharing ID share the same data. The sharing ID is unique to the shared data during the lifetime of the object in the session.

member.name: M:VisualComponents.Create3D.ISimNode.MeasureDistance(VisualComponents.Create3D.ISimNode[])
member.summary: Measure closest distance to other node(s).

remarks.para: This method measures the distance from this node to one or more other nodes. The distance is based on the closest points between geometry in the nodes.
If the distance cannot be obtained (for example if there is no geometry to measure in the node or nodes) the result is null.
Otherwise, a result object is returned, with coordinates set relative to this node.

member.returns: Minimum distance to other nodes, or null if not found.

member.name: E:VisualComponents.Create3D.ISimWorld.NodeTreeFinalized
member.summary: Raised when one or more simulation nodes are to be added to the world. This event is not raised for dynamic components.

remarks.para: This event is raised in the following situations:

list.item: When a model is loaded, this event is raised once for all loaded components.
When a component is created, either through the API or by cloning or during simulation, this event is raised once for the newly created component.
When a node is created through the API, this event is raised once for the node.
When a legacy node is upgraded as a result of changing its JointExpression or PivotExpression properties through the API, this event is raised once for the node.

remarks.para: When this event is raised during component creation or loading, it is raised before any component names are changed to avoid naming conflicts.

member.name: T:VisualComponents.Create3D.ICollisionDetector
member.summary: Collision detector layout item interface.

remarks.para: The collision detector is a layout item that tests for collisions between two groups of nodes. These groups are defined as node lists, where each entry may include or exclude a single simulation node, component, or node subtree.

Depending on settings, the detector can highlight the colliding nodes during simulation, or stop the simulation if a collision is detected. It can also be used to test for collisions programmatically through this interface.

member.summary: Whether to calculate minimum distance between the collision lists.

member.name: P:VisualComponents.Create3D.ICollisionDetector.Tolerance
member.summary: Collision detection threshold distance. Cannot be negative value.

remarks.para: A collision is registered when the smallest distance between geometries in list A and list B is less than this value.

Note: If Tolerance is set to zero, a simplified collision detection algorithm is used. This algorithm does not detect collisions if one geometry is completely enclosed by the other, i.e. if the bounding box surfaces do not intersect.

member.summary: Test for collisions and return the first collision.

remarks.para: This method stops testing after finding the first collision.

member.returns: The first detected collision, or an empty collection if no collisions were detected.

member.name: M:VisualComponents.Create3D.ICollisionDetector.TestAllCollisions
member.summary: Test for collisions and return all detected collision instances.
member.returns: All detected collisions, or an empty collection if no collisions were detected.

member.name: M:VisualComponents.Create3D.ICollisionDetector.TestMinimumDistance(System.Double)
member.summary: Compute minimum distance between node lists

remarks.para: This method tests all nodes that are within the specified maximum range of each other, and returns a record of the minimum distance between the nodes.
If the minimum distance is greater than the maximum range, no result is returned.
Calling this method will not automatically display result indicator in UI if is set to false. In this case this need to be explicitly requested by publishing with the returned collision records.

member.returns: Minimum distance information, or an empty collection if the maximum range was exceeded.

member.name: M:VisualComponents.Create3D.ICollisionDetector.TestAllIntersections
member.summary: Test for collisions and return all detected collision instances.

remarks.para: It collects all intersecting triangles as well as intersecting points between those triangles.

member.returns: Minimum distance information, or an empty collection if the maximum range was exceeded.

member.summary: Test for collisions between simulation node bound boxes only.

remarks.para: This is faster than geometry based collision testing, but not as accurate.

member.summary: Modifiable property list object that is saved with a layout.

member.name: P:VisualComponents.Create3D.ILayoutPropertyList.Class
member.summary:
Gets or sets the property list class name. Class string determines what happens when the layout is imported into an existing layout.
If Class is an empty string, the property list is added to the existing layout. If the layout already has another layout item with the same name, the name of the new item is modified to avoid a name collision.
If Class is not empty, and the existing layout has a layout property list with the same Class string, then the property values of the existing layout item are updated with the values from the layout being loaded. In this case, no new layout item is created.
The default value for the Class property is an empty string.

member.name: E:VisualComponents.Create3D.ILayoutSchemaPropertyList.RecordAppended
member.summary: Occurs when a record (row) has been appended to a schema.
member.remarks: Append is defined by the inserted records being located at the end of a schema, allowing the freedom not to consider following records (rows), if the data is sequential in nature (e.g. a sequence of positions). Hence, to comply with this notion, the first record inserted to an empty schema is considered as being "appended".

member.name: T:VisualComponents.Create3D.ISweptVolume
member.summary: Swept volume layout item interface.
member.para: The ISweptVolume defines the list of nodes that is used for generating a swept volume (volume displacement). Swept Volume requires at least one node list. A swept volume is being recorded during simulation time when the nodes of the selected component are moving. The list of nodes is transformed into one or more convex hulls upon movement, an iterative process ensues, and the swept volume from the convex hulls is generated in the 3D world.

member.name: P:VisualComponents.Create3D.ISweptVolume.NodeList
member.summary: Node list.

member.name: M:VisualComponents.Create3D.ISweptVolume.SetNodeList(System.Collections.Generic.IEnumerable{VisualComponents.Create3D.NodeListEntry})
member.summary: Set the node list.

remarks.para: This clears the current node list and populates it with the given node entries.

member.name: P:VisualComponents.Create3D.ISweptVolume.TargetNode
member.summary: Defines the node where the geometry generated by the swept volume is stored. The target node position should remain static during the simulation.

member.name: P:VisualComponents.Create3D.ISweptVolume.Representation
member.summary: Indicates how the list node will be represented when doing the swept volume.

member.name: P:VisualComponents.Create3D.ISweptVolume.Method
member.summary: Indicates the method to be used when doing the swept volume.

member.name: P:VisualComponents.Create3D.ISweptVolume.DecompositionQuality
member.summary: If the Structure property is set equal to Decomposition, the quality of that decomposition can be set from a range of 0 to 100.

member.name: P:VisualComponents.Create3D.ISweptVolume.DecompositionDecimationTarget
member.summary: If the Structure property is set equal to Decomposition, a decimation target can be set to expedite/speed up the process. Decimation target refers to the number of triangle sets remaining after the decimation process. This process only applies to nodes with fewer triangle sets than the decimation target. Set to 0 for no effect.

member.name: P:VisualComponents.Create3D.ISweptVolume.Material
member.summary: Material of the created swept volume. If set to null, the swept volume will try to get the material from the swept geometry

member.summary: Start point of the swept volume process. The Structure is initiated during this call. The center of each node's boundary is used.

member.summary: Start point of the swept volume process. The Structure is initiated during this call.

member.summary: Iterative process that creates the visual swept volume based on positions. the center of each node's boundary is used.

member.summary: Iterative process that creates the visual swept volume based on positions.
member.param: If null, the center of each node's boundary is used.

member.name: M:VisualComponents.Create3D.ISweptVolume.End
member.summary: Finishes the swept volume. Capping of the swept volume can be done at this stage if needed.

member.name: M:VisualComponents.Create3D.ISweptVolume.Clear
member.summary: Clears the geometry generated by the swept volume, which can be done during a simulation.

member.name: M:VisualComponents.Create3D.ISweptVolume.Store
member.summary: Stores geometry generated by swept volume in TargetNode after the end of a swept volume process. If no geometry is generated during a swept volume process, no feature is created and the method returns null. You should call this method after executing the end() method as well as before executing the clear() method.
member.returns: feature that contains the stored swept volume.

summary.para: Returns true is is currently holding a handle to this license.

This is important for local licenses, because each handle reserves a new seat. Therefore, if the service is already holding a handle to e.g. the main product feature's license, then we will likely fail if we try to get another one.
Will check if license(s) are available for all given feature(s).
If is false, this will acquire and return said licenses, that then need to be released by the caller.

member.name: T:VisualComponents.Create3D.ILicenseHandle
member.summary: License handle interface.

remarks.para: The implementation of this interface retains a license handle during its lifetime, making it unavailable for use by other computers in case the license is a network license.
The license is released once the handle is disposed.
A license handle can be tested to see if it is still valid. See for a description of the challenge-response mechanism.

remarks.para: This will throw an exception if the license is no longer valid.

member.name: T:VisualComponents.Create3D.ILicensingChallenge
member.summary: Licensing challenge interface.

remarks.para: The licensing challenge interface is used for the VC proprietary challenge-response mechanism. The implementation provides a challenge string through the Challenge property, and receives a Response string during the operation. The implementation must then verify that the response is correct, and based on that decide whether to continue the operation.

member.name: T:VisualComponents.Create3D.ILicensingService
member.summary: Licensing service interface.

remarks.para: This interface is to a service that aggregates all license requests so that each feature is allocated only once. It is intended for use by the .NET-side UI and/or code elements that need licensing protection.

To protect code with a license, before running, make sure to get a license handle using one of the getters. Add-ons should use GetAddOnLicense. It is recommended that the handle be retained until the end of the session, and then disposed.

example.para: Example using the licensing service to protect licensed code:

member.name: M:VisualComponents.Create3D.ILicensingService.GetMainLicense(System.String,VisualComponents.Create3D.ILicensingChallenge)
member.summary: Get main product feature license.

remarks.para:
The differences between this and are:
Main licenses always have the same version string as the main application, whereas add-on licenses specify their own version strings.
If a valid license is not found, this method will close the application while the other won't.

member.name: E:VisualComponents.Create3D.ILicensingService.LicenseCheckFailed
member.summary: Raised when a license check has failed.

remarks.para: This event is raised when e.g. the connection to the license server is lost. It contains a countdown parameter indicating how many times this event will be called before the software shuts down.
If there is a problem with the license check, this event will be raised every second, until the countdown reaches zero, at which point the software will exit.
If the error condition is remedied, LicenseCheckSucceeded will be raised once to indicate this.

member.name: E:VisualComponents.Create3D.ILicensingService.LicenseCheckSucceeded
member.summary: Raised when a license check has succeeded, after it has failed.

remarks.para: This event is raised only after LicenseCheckFailed has been raised, and the error condition has been remedied, e.g. if LicenseCheckFailed was raised because the connection to the license server was lost, this event is raised once the connection is restored.

If the return value is null, the ConnectionCheckCompleted event will be raised when the connection check has completed. The status can then be read from ConnectionStatus.
It is recommended to add a handler to ConnectionCheckCompleted before this method is called in order to avoid missing the event if the check completes quickly.

Exports with this type of metadata are not instantiated if the required features are not present in the current license configuration.
Note that this check is only done for multiple import type exports.
The required features can be specified as any of the following:

item.description:

member.name: T:VisualComponents.Create3D.IPathObjectNode
member.summary: Path object node interface.There are four different types of nodes in the IvcPathObject. These include action nodes, motion nodes, parameter nodes and reference nodes. A reference node is comparable with a base frame in robotics. It may be relative to a simulation node. It may also be relative to the world origin. If it is relative to a simulation node, it follows the simulation node if it moves. Motion nodes and parameter nodes may be relative to reference node. If so, then they move when reference node moves. Action nodes are relative to motion nodes but their physical location in 3D space is defined by the trajectory segment. So its location depends on LogicalDistance property, that in turn is calculated from the LogicalDistance of the motion node it is relative to and Offset value.
member.remarks: Path object has been deprecated in 4.0. This interface should be only used to retrieve the data from layouts saved in the previous versions.

member.name: M:VisualComponents.Create3D.Robotics.Shadow.IFastShadowRobotScope.Inverse(VisualComponents.Create3D.Matrix,System.Int32,System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlyCollection{System.Double})

summary.para: Calculate inverse kinematics.
Returns true if the calculation was succesfull. The results can then be read from .
If this method returns false, call to get more information.

member.param: The target matrix that the kinematic structure attemps to reach. Target is given in the active base coordinates

Starting values for joints. Null can be given to use previously provided values (or zeros if called the first time). The list of joint values must contain all joints starting with internal (robot) joints, followed by external joint values. The order is the same as in the original robot controller. External joint values are solved first, meaning that the given values are considered as the target/final position instead of initial/start.
member.exception: May be thrown by implementations that require initializating, if that object has not yet been initialized.

member.name: P:VisualComponents.Create3D.IJoint.Value
member.summary: Current joint value.

remarks.para: The unit of the joint value depends on the joint type. Conventionally, for rotational joints, the joint value is expressed in degrees, and for linear joints the value is expressed in millimeters.
This can be changed by modelling the servo or robot to use joint values in a different way; however, in that case, the following points must be observed:

item.description: In the case of servo controllers, all motions are joint value based, and the unit has no impact. The only exception is that turns of rotational joints are calculated based on degrees; however, this only affects the turn number seen through the API and has no impact on motion calculation, so it is safe to ignore.
In the case of robots, all the built-in kinematics types assume that the joints are expressed in degrees or millimeters, so changing the units requires a custom Python kinematic object.

In robots, there is also turn calculation for rotational joints, but here they are also subject to turn selection which affects the robot movement in some cases. Since the joint turn system assumes that the unit is degrees, in order to change the unit, the turn calculation must be disabled and handled manually in the custom kinematic object.

member.summary: Indicates that robot should move through this point without decelerating. Note: this flag is usable only in rare cases. There are few demands for it to work nicely: - external joints must not move. - both previous and next movement targets must be linear. - distance of the previous and next movements should be similar. - orientation of previous/this/next movement targets should be similar.

summary.para: This interface allows direct access to an RCS module.
Users are encouraged to use and instead.

member.name: M:VisualComponents.Create3D.Rrs.IDirectRcsAccess.CallRcs``2(``0,System.String)

summary.para: Calls a loaded RCS module with the given input data and returns the output returned by the RCS module.

The input and output data types must be laid out in memory in the exact format that is required by the RRS specification. This API specifically expects that the input data begins with a three-integer header and the output data begins with a one-integer header.

When defining the struct types, it is recommended to use the StructLayout attribute with parameters (LayoutKind.Sequential, Pack = 1, CharSet = CharSet.Ansi). For string members inside the struct, it is recommended to use [MarshalAs(UnmanagedType.ByValTStr, SizeConst = N)], where N is the maximum size for your string.

member.typeparam: Type of input data. Must be laid out in memory according to the RRS-I specification and must include the input header.
Type of output data. Must be laid out in memory according to the RRS-I specification and must include the output header.
member.param: Input data that will be sent to the RCS module.
The name of the method you are calling, to be used e.g. for logging. Value can be null.

member.name: T:VisualComponents.Create3D.Rrs.RrsEventType
member.summary: Holds known constant identifier values for RRS-I event types.
member.remarks: This feature is only available in Visual Components Premium or KUKA.Sim.

summary.para: EventSpec(1) specifies the time in milliseconds.
A negative or zero value specifies time before or at the specified target, a positive value specifies time after the specified target.
EventSpec(1) specifies the distance in mm.
A negative value specifies distance before the specified target, a positive value specifies distance after the specified target.
EventSpec(1) specifies the time in milliseconds; see .
EventSpec(2) specifies the distance in mm; see .
EventSpec(1) Specifies the condition direction (ConditionAxis).

Can be one of the following values.
1 X
2 Y
3 Z
EventSpec(2) specifies the condition type (ConditionType).

Can be one of the following values.
0 greater than
1 less than
EventSpec(3) specifies the condition value (ConditionValue) in mm.
EventSpec(1) specifies the distance in percentages.
It may be positive (after target) or negative (before target).
EventSpec(1) specifies the time in milliseconds; see .
EventSpec(2) specifies the distance in percentages; see .

member.name: F:VisualComponents.Create3D.ChartTileState.MinimizedExpanded
member.summary: 'MinimizedExpanded' is only returned if there is at least one tile in a 'Maximized' state. A Tile in the 'MinimizedExpanded' state will usually display its Header and its Content but the Tile will be grouped with all other minimized Tiles, both collapsed and expanded.

member.summary: Constructor.

member.name: P:VisualComponents.Create3D.ConnectionEditorConfigElement.ChangeSelectionOnComponentDoubleClick
member.summary: If this is enabled, double-clicking a component in 3D World will change the currently selected component to the one you double-clicked. If the option is disabled, all clicks will be interpreted as single clicks.

member.name: P:VisualComponents.Create3D.ConnectionEditorConfigElement.ChangeSelectionOnNodeTitleDoubleClick
member.summary: If this is enabled, double-clicking the node's title will change the currently selected component to a component which the double-clicked node represents.

member.name: P:VisualComponents.Create3D.ConnectionEditorConfigElement.AllowConnectionDragging
member.summary: If this is enabled, connections can be dragged out of connectors and dropped on other connectors or components (interfaces) and buttons/check-boxes to show or hide connection lines will be available. If this is disabled, those buttons will be hidden and it will not be possible to drag connections.

member.name: P:VisualComponents.Create3D.ConnectionEditorConfigElement.ShowOnlyMatchingInterfaces
member.summary: If this is enabled, only interfaces that can be connected to the selected interface will be shown in the nodes. All interfaces will be shown otherwise.

member.name: P:VisualComponents.Create3D.ConnectionEditorConfigElement.InterfacesNodeVisibilityThreshold
member.summary: The number of matching interfaces a node must contain in order to be shown. For example, if the value of this option is 2 and a certain node contains 5 interfaces, but only one interface can be connecte to the selected interface, that node will be hidden. [Requires InterfacesNodeExpansionMode == Locked].

member.name: P:VisualComponents.Create3D.ConnectionEditorConfigElement.InterfacesListItemAlternativeNamingThreshold
member.summary: The number of matching interfaces a node must contain to have connections (to it) in the list represented with alternative (includes interface's name in the brackets) name. For example, if the value of this option is 2 and a certain node has 2 interfaces that are already connected or can be connected to the selected node, then the corresponding connections in the list will be represented as component name + interface name.

member.name: P:VisualComponents.Create3D.ConnectionEditorConfigElement.ShowInterfacesNetworkMapByDefault
member.summary: Determines the default value of the "Show Network Map" checbox in Interfaces action.

member.name: P:VisualComponents.Create3D.ConnectionEditorConfigElement.ShowSignalsNetworkMapByDefault
member.summary: Determines the default value of the "Show Network Map" checbox in Signals action.

member.name: P:VisualComponents.Create3D.ConnectionEditorConfigElement.InterfacesNodeExpansionMode
member.summary:
Controls how and which nodes in the Interfaces Network Map will be expanded. Available values:
All - All nodes will be expanded by default. Every node can be collapsed and expanded again.
Connected - Main node and all nodes that have at least one connection to any other node will be expanded.
ConnectedToMain - Main node and all nodes that have at least one connection to the main node will be expanded.
Locked - Expanding/collapsing nodes is not possible. Corresponding buttons will be hidden from the UI and collapsed nodes will be hidden from the view.
Main - Only main node will be expanded. Every node can be collapsed and expanded again.

member.name: P:VisualComponents.Create3D.ConnectionEditorConfigElement.SignalsNodeExpansionMode
member.summary:
Controls how and which nodes in the Signals Network Map will be expanded. Available values:
All - All nodes will be expanded by default. Every node can be collapsed and expanded again.
Connected - Main node and all nodes that have at least one connection to any other node will be expanded.
ConnectedToMain - Main node and all nodes that have at least one connection to the main node will be expanded.
Main - Only main node will be expanded. Every node can be collapsed and expanded again.

member.name: P:VisualComponents.Create3D.ConnectionEditorConfigElement.InterfacesNodePinningMode
member.summary:
Controls whether and how pinning of the nodes in Interfaces Network Map will be preserved. Available values:
PreserveOnActionDeactivate - Pinned nodes will remain pinned even if you cancel the Interfaces Action. Every node can be pinned/unpinned manually.Pinning will be reset only on application restart.
PreserveOnComponentChange - Pinned nodes will remain pinned even if you change the selected component. Closing the panel (cancels the Action) will reset all pinning. Every node can be pinned/unpinned manually.
PreserveOnInterfaceChange - Pinned nodes will remain pinned even if you change the selected interface. Changing the selected component or closing the panel will reset all pinning. Nodes can be pinned/unpinned manually.
ResetOnNodeVisibilityChange - Same as PreserveOnInterfaceChange, but pinning will be reset for nodes that are hidden from the view. For example, if ShowOnlyMatchingInterfaces option is enabled, some nodes might have no matching interface if you change the selected interface and thus will be hidden. Pinning of such nodes will be preserved with PreserveOnInterfaceChange option, but with this option they will be unpinned. Changing the selected component or closing the panel will reset all pinning. Nodes can be pinned/unpinned manually.
DoNotPreserve - Pinned nodes will remain pinned only on basic actions (i.e.connect/disconnect, drag connection, etc.). Changing the selected interface/component or closing the panel will reset all pinning.Nodes can be pinned/unpinned manually.
Disabled - Pinning is completely disabled. Nodes can be pinned/unpinned only programmatically. The corresponding button will be hidden from the UI.

member.name: P:VisualComponents.Create3D.ConnectionEditorConfigElement.SignalsNodePinningMode
member.summary:
Controls whether and how pinning of the nodes in Signals Network Map will be preserved. Available values:
PreserveOnActionDeactivate - Pinned nodes will remain pinned even if you cancel the Signals Action. Every node can be pinned/unpinned manually. Pinning will be reset only on application restart.
PreserveOnComponentChange - Pinned nodes will remain pinned even if you change the selected component. Closing the panel (cancels the Action) will reset all pinning. Every node can be pinned/unpinned manually.
PreserveOnSignalChange - Pinned nodes will remain pinned even if you change the selected signal. Changing the selected component or closing the panel will reset all pinning. Nodes can be pinned/unpinned manually.
ResetOnNodeVisibilityChange - Same as PreserveOnSignalChange, but pinning will be reset for nodes that are hidden from the view. For example, if ShowOnlyMatchingInterfaces option is enabled, some nodes might have no matching interface if you change the selected interface and thus will be hidden. Pinning of such nodes will be preserved with PreserveOnInterfaceChange option, but with this option they will be unpinned. Changing the selected component or closing the panel will reset all pinning. Nodes can be pinned/unpinned manually.
DoNotPreserve - Pinned nodes will remain pinned only on basic actions (i.e.connect/disconnect, drag connection, etc.). Changing the selected interface/component or closing the panel will reset all pinning.Nodes can be pinned/unpinned manually.
Disabled - Pinning is completely disabled. Nodes can be pinned/unpinned only programmatically. The corresponding button will be hidden from the UI.

member.name: P:VisualComponents.Create3D.ConnectionEditorConfigElement.UseSimplifiedMaterialInGhostMode
member.summary: Defines whether components in ghost-mode should be rendered with a simple solid gray material or using a semi- transparent ghost material calculated from their original materials. If this option is enabled, ghost component highlighting will happen faster and will not have a significant performance impact on 3D World navigation.

member.name: P:VisualComponents.Create3D.ConnectionEditorConfigElement.EnableNodeVirtualization
member.summary: Defines whether UI virtualization is enabled in a canvas that hosts the Network Map.

member.name: P:VisualComponents.Create3D.ConnectionEditorConfigElement.IndirectInterfaceConnectionsVisibility
member.summary:
Determines if the Network Map should contain (and show) connections going from/to an adjacent component to another adjacent component or another interface of the selected component. This option affects only Network Map and is useless when AllowConnectionDragging option is disabled. Available values:
All - All indirect connections from/to all components in the 3D World which have the corresponding node in the Network Map will be shown.
Component - Indirect connections between adjacent components (components that have at least one interface which can be or is already connected to any of interfaces in selected component) will be shown.
Interface - Only indirect connections from/to interfaces of the selected component will be shown.
None - No indirect connections will be shown.

Services/messages and their managers/servers:
- handshake - HandshakeServer.cs/cpp (todo) - establishing the connection.
- stream - StreamServer.cs/cpp (todo) - serializing the whole layout. Keeping it in sync in the viewer side. - processed by Experience or ThreeJs viewer.
- base - BaseServer.cs
- vr_events - VREventsServer.cs - sending/receiving VR events and tracking data.
Ports: - 6688 - VC.Engine.exe - 7000 - VC.Headless.exe / VC.Engine.exe - 700x - VC.Headless.exe
